claims.claim: Collect vSphere diagnostic bundles: vm-support on ESXi, vc-support on VCSA, from the client or API
claims.note: Frontmatter description scope: KB 1010705 confirms only the vm-support-on-ESXi half ("The command-line vm-support utility is present on all versions of VMware ESXi"); neither listed source mentions vc-support, VCSA or an API collection path.

claims.evidence_quote: To export the log bundle to a specific shared vmfs datastore, use this command: vm-support -w /vmfs/volumes/DATASTORE_NAME

claims.note: KB 1010705 says vm-support "produces a gzipped tarball ( .tgz file) locally on the host" but neither source states the esx-<host>-<date> filename pattern.

Neither KB documents vm-support's -p/-d/-i performance-snapshot flags or the 300 s / 10 s values; KB 653 covers only the vSphere Client's "Gather performance data" option with a duration and interval.

claims.evidence_quote: Using any HTTP client, download the resource from: https://ESXHostnameOrIPAddress/cgi-bin/vm-support.cgi

claims.claim:
Actions → Export System Logs → select hosts (and optionally vCenter), include
performance data if relevant
claims.evidence_quote: Right click the vCenter object and select Export System Logs . Select All or only the desired ESXi host to collect logs at the same time.
claims.note: The same KB section also has "If required, select Include vCenter Server and vSphere UI logs ." and "If required, select the Gather performance data option, and specify a duration and interval."

claims.claim:
Write to a datastore, not `/tmp` (RAM disk, may fill and
hurt the host)
claims.note: Neither KB warns against /tmp or calls it a RAM disk; KB 1010705 only says that without -w vm-support picks a VMFS or VFFS partition with the highest free space, listing /var/tmp/, /var/log/ and the working directory as possible locations.

claims.claim: vc-support -l           # on VCSA shell, writes to /storage/log by default
claims.note: Neither listed source mentions vc-support, the VCSA shell or /storage/log; both articles cover ESXi host diagnostics only.
Neither listed source mentions the appliance support-bundle URL or VAMI; both articles cover ESXi host diagnostics only.

claims.claim:
Bundles can be
GBs; check `/storage/log` free space first (`df -h`)
claims.note: Neither listed source mentions bundle sizes, /storage/log or df -h.

claims.claim: hostd/vmkernel logs rotate within days on busy hosts
claims.note: Neither listed source mentions log rotation, hostd or vmkernel logs.

claims.claim: Note the UTC time of the incident; logs are in UTC
claims.note: Neither listed source mentions UTC or log timestamps.

claims.claim: For a PSOD, collect after the host returns: the core dump is extracted into the bundle
claims.note: Neither listed source covers PSOD collection or core-dump extraction into the bundle; KB 653 only offers a "Password for encrypted core dumps" option in the export dialog.

claims.claim: as long as a dump target was configured
claims.note: Dump-target prerequisite for the PSOD core dump; neither listed source mentions dump targets.

claims.claim:
Use the Broadcom support portal upload for the case, or the vendor's file transfer
service
claims.evidence_quote: Upload the logs to the Broadcom Support Portal.
claims.note: KB 1010705 covers the transfer-service half: "After the log bundle is collected and downloaded to a client, upload the logs to the SFTP/FTP site ."

claims.claim:
Strip nothing yourself, but be aware bundles contain hostnames, IPs, and
usernames
claims.note: Both KBs say only "Data collected in a host support bundle may be considered sensitive"; neither enumerates hostnames, IPs and usernames.

claims.claim:
copy the relevant logs only:
`scp root@<host>:/var/log/{vmkernel,hostd,vobd}.log .` and the VM's `vmware.log`
claims.note: Neither source covers copying individual vmkernel/hostd/vobd logs or vmware.log; KB 1010705 says only that the collected bundle "can be copied off the host using FTP, SCP, or another method".

claims.claim: Bundle opens (`tar tzf` lists `var/log/*` and `commands/*` outputs)
claims.note: Neither listed source describes the bundle's internal layout or tar tzf verification.

claims.claim:
its time range covers
the incident, and the case has the upload reference
claims.note: Verify-section criterion; neither listed source mentions checking a bundle's time range or an upload reference.

coverage: I chose every concrete claim in the skill - the frontmatter description's collection scope, both vm-support command lines (the -w datastore destination and the -p -d 300 -i 10 performance snapshot), the esx-<host>-<date>.tgz output name, the vm-support.cgi browser URL, the vSphere Client Export System Logs flow with host selection and optional vCenter logs, the /tmp RAM-disk warning, vc-support -l with its /storage/log default, the appliance/support-bundle URL and VAMI, the GBs / df -h free-space check, the log-rotation window and UTC timing, the PSOD core-dump claim, the portal/transfer-service upload, the bundle-contents warning, the scp partial-collection command and both Verify criteria (tar tzf layout, time range and upload reference) - covering every command, flag, URL, path, number and behaviour, and checked each against both listed Broadcom KB articles, which together confirm only the ESXi-side items (vm-support -w, the vm-support.cgi download, the Export System Logs flow and the portal upload) and cover none of the VCSA, performance-flag, timing or bundle-content claims.
suggested_edits: Nothing is contradicted, but both listed KBs are ESXi-host articles, so the skill's vCenter half and several operational claims are unsourced. Add fetchable sources for vc-support on the VCSA shell (the -l flag and /storage/log default), the https://<vcsa>/appliance/support-bundle URL and VAMI (a vCenter support-bundle KB or the VAMI documentation), vm-support's -p/-d/-i performance-snapshot flags and values, the esx-<host>-<date>.tgz bundle naming, and bundle contents (KB 653 already links 'Data collected when gathering diagnostic information from vSphere products', which would cover the hostnames/IPs/usernames warning); either source or drop the /tmp RAM-disk warning, the log-rotation window, the UTC note and the PSOD/dump-target claim. The scp and tar tzf verification steps can stay as reviewer technique but remain unverifiable unless a source documents them.
